name: Protective Call (short-stock hedge)
summary: Hold a short stock position and buy a call against it to cap the unlimited upside risk. The mirror image of a protective put; obscure in retail practice.

legs.strike_rule: Delta 0.20-0.30, strike above the short entry

max_loss: (call strike - short entry + call debit) x 100. This converts an unlimited-risk short into a defined-risk one.
breakevens: short entry price - call debit per share

greeks.delta: -100 from the short plus +20 to +30 from the call = -70 to -80 net

when_to_use: Only if the system ever carries short equity - which it should not. Documented so the machine knows the correct repair if an unintended short appears, e.g. from an auto-exercised long put.
entry_rules: Requires an existing short equity position, which this system does not intend to hold

If an unintended short stock position appears (auto-exercised long put), the FIRST action is to buy the shares back, not to hedge with a call. Use this only if the buyback cannot be executed immediately (halt, no liquidity)
Call delta 0.20-0.30, 30-90 DTE, nearest liquid strike above the short entry
management_rules: Treat as a temporary bandage: close the entire structure within 1 trading day
Roll the call down as the short becomes profitable, in 0.20-0.30 delta increments
exit_rules: Close the short stock and sell the call within 1 trading day of establishing the hedge
If the call is ITM at expiry it auto-exercises and BUYS 100 shares, closing the short - acceptable but not a plan
assignment_risk: None on the call (you are long it). The short stock itself carries hard-to-borrow, buy-in and dividend-liability risk.
buying_power: Short stock margin (50% Reg T initial) plus the call debit. Short equity is not permitted under normal operation of this system.
common_mistakes: Using this as an excuse to tolerate a short stock position rather than flattening it immediately.
